6. Submit the request. Removal is not instant -- check back periodically, since Whitepages/411 listings can reappear after new data pulls.

brokers.name: Arrests.org
brokers.opt_out_email: <verify: removal contact email is Cloudflare-email-protected on third-party guides, literal address not independently confirmed>
brokers.notes: WebFetch of arrests.org returned HTTP 403 (site live, actively bot-blocking). Multiple independent 2025-2026 removal guides (Incogni, Onerep, PurePrivacy, idstrong, EXPOSE, mugshotremovalservice) converge on the same mechanism: a mugshot/arrest-record aggregator organized by state; removal via a per-listing form at arrests.org/remove/?id=<RecordID> (Record ID taken from your listing's URL), where you select a removal reason (charges dropped/not adjudicated guilty, sealed/expunged, or 'remove my date of birth and address') and upload a redacted government photo ID (name/DOB/photo visible, other fields blacked out) plus supporting court documentation if applicable. An alternate email-based route is described by multiple guides but the literal address is Cloudflare-email-protected in every source found and could not be confirmed -- left as a <verify:> placeholder rather than guessed. Guides consistently state removal itself is free ('Arrests.org doesn't charge for it, but it does require photo ID verification'), but also consistently warn that paid 'expedited removal' resellers have historically marked up what should be a free process -- charges_fee left false per the site's own stated policy, with a strong do-not-pay warning in the instructions below. Processing 5-30 days. gov_id + guided tier reflect the photo-ID upload requirement; legal_basis left [none] since no CCPA/GDPR opt-out-of-sale framing was found -- this is a direct takedown-request process, not a statutory data-sale opt-out. last_verified left null.
brokers.instructions_md:
1. Find your listing on arrests.org and copy the Record ID from its URL.
2. Go to the removal form, following the pattern https://arrests.org/remove/?id=<your Record ID> (replace with the ID from step 1).
3. Select the removal reason that applies to you: charges were dropped/not adjudicated guilty, the arrest was sealed or expunged, or you're only requesting removal of your date of birth and address from the listing.
4. Upload a redacted copy of a government-issued photo ID -- black out everything except your name, date of birth, and photo -- plus any supporting court documents (expungement order, disposition record) relevant to your selected reason.
5. Submit the form and allow 5-30 days for a decision; Arrests.org does not always grant removal requests and may not remove all associated data even when it does.
6. Do not pay anyone for "expedited" removal -- legitimate removal through Arrests.org's own process is free, and paid resellers offering faster removal have been reported as a markup scheme, not an official service.
7. Removing the listing here is a privacy/visibility fix only -- the underlying arrest record remains in official court and police databases until you separately expunge or seal it through the court system.

**Sensitive-data note:** this process requires uploading a (redacted) government photo ID. Only proceed if you're comfortable sharing that; there's no lower-friction alternative documented.

brokers.name: Backgroundchecks.com LLC
brokers.notes: WebFetch on backgroundchecks.com/privacypolicy rendered directly and confirmed the CCPA process: email info@backgroundchecks.com with full name, all physical addresses on file, all email addresses, all phone numbers, all employers, and a legible image of a government-issued ID showing a California address. The policy itself notes the CCPA does not strictly apply to their FCRA-governed background-screening business, but they operate this opt-out mechanism anyway. Government-ID requirement pushes this to guided tier despite the plain-email method (method:email normally implies auto, but the id_required gate overrides that here). Background-check broker reselling records on named individuals -> people_search true, crucial priority.
brokers.instructions_md:
1. Email info@backgroundchecks.com stating you are exercising your CCPA right to opt out of the sale/sharing of your personal information (and/or requesting deletion).
2. In the same email, include: your full name, every physical address associated with your record, every email address on file, every phone number on file, and every employer listed.
3. Attach a legible image of a government-issued ID showing your California address -- Backgroundchecks.com requires this to verify your identity before acting on the request.
4. If your concern is about the accuracy of an FCRA background-check report rather than a CCPA sale opt-out, use their disputes page at backgroundchecks.com/disputes instead, which follows FCRA dispute procedures.
5. Keep a copy of your email and ID submission for your records, and follow up if you don't receive confirmation within a reasonable time.

brokers.name: BustedMugshots.com
brokers.opt_out_url: <verify: locate the current removal-policy/FAQ page on bustedmugshots.com -- not reliably reachable via automated fetch (TLS errors)>
brokers.notes: BustedMugshots.com aggregates and publishes arrest-record mugshots and is a well-documented mugshot-broker site. Multiple independent opt-out guides (Comparitech, DeleteMe, Incogni, InternetPrivacy) consistently describe the same narrow removal path: the site states it does not accept payment for removal and is not currently processing general removal requests, but will remove listings for cases that were sealed, expunged, resulted in acquittal/dismissal, or where the subject is deceased -- if the requester supplies supporting court/legal documentation via help@bustedmugshots.com. This is a documentation-gated process (not a plain opt-out), so classified tier:guided despite method:email, and id_required:true because court/legal documents (functionally government-issued proof) are required. Direct WebFetch of bustedmugshots.com pages failed with TLS/certificate errors during research, so this is reconstructed from third-party guides rather than a freshly rendered page; opt_out_url left as a verify placeholder and last_verified is null.
brokers.instructions_md:
1. Determine whether your case qualifies: BustedMugshots.com states it will only remove listings where the case was sealed, expunged, you were found not guilty, the charges were dismissed, or the subject is deceased. It does not offer general removal and does not accept payment for removal.
2. Gather supporting documentation proving your case qualifies -- e.g. a court order of expungement/sealing, a dismissal record, or (for a deceased subject) a certified death certificate.
3. Email help@bustedmugshots.com with your full name, a link to your specific listing on the site, and the supporting documentation attached.
4. Keep your request factual, polite, and non-threatening -- removal in qualifying cases is reportedly handled at the site's discretion.
5. If your case does not meet one of these narrow criteria, BustedMugshots.com is unlikely to remove your listing directly; consider a broader reputation-management/suppression strategy instead.
6. Because BustedMugshots.com is only one of many mugshot-aggregator sites, a successful removal here will not remove copies of the same mugshot from other, separately operated mugshot sites -- each requires its own request.

If your case instead ended favorably (not guilty, dismissal, acquittal, exoneration, pardon, nolle prosequi, adjudication withheld) or you completed all obligations of a non-favorable disposition (fines paid, probation finished, time served), Mugshots.com will update -- not remove -- the listing to reflect that outcome.

Yasni (operated by yasni GmbH, Frankfurt, Germany) is a people-search/identity-aggregation site that indexes public web content (professional profiles, mentions, etc.) under a person's name and also lets individuals create/claim a self-authored profile ('Exposé'). The privacy page states data-subject erasure requests go to datenschutz@yasni.de (the company's data-protection contact); the help page separately gives info@yasni.de for deleting a self-created Exposé/account, with Yasni confirming deletion by email once processed. Yasni's own guidance for search-result content sourced from elsewhere on the web is to contact the original publishing site rather than Yasni directly -- so this opt-out most reliably covers Yasni-hosted Exposé profiles, not every underlying source. Used the data-protection address (datenschutz@yasni.de) as the primary opt_out_email since it is the GDPR-erasure-specific contact; info@yasni.de is a workable alternative noted in the instructions. No CAPTCHA/form/ID requirement found -> tier:auto. GDPR is the clear legal basis (EU entity); CCPA not confirmed to apply. last_verified left null.
brokers.instructions_md:
1. Search your name on yasni.com and note the URLs of any Yasni-hosted profile pages ("Exposé") or search-result entries that show your information.
2. Email datenschutz@yasni.de (Yasni's data-protection contact) and state that you are exercising your GDPR right to erasure/objection, listing the profile URL(s) you found and your full name.
3. If you specifically created or claimed a self-authored Exposé/account on Yasni and want it deleted, you can instead (or additionally) email info@yasni.de with a short deletion request -- Yasni states it will confirm by email once your account/Exposé is deleted.
4. For search results that summarize content originally published on a different website (not a Yasni-hosted profile), Yasni's own guidance is that removal must be requested from that original source site, since Yasni does not control or store that content itself -- only re-indexes it.
5. Keep the confirmation email as proof of your request; Yasni does not publish a stated processing timeline, so follow up if you don't hear back within a few weeks.

brokers.name: Alarms California (licensedata.org network)
brokers.notes: alarmscalifornia.org is an independent, unofficial directory (not a state agency) that republishes California alarm agent/company license records sourced from the Bureau of Security and Investigative Services, with a search/browse UI and customer reviews -- confirming the prior pass's finding that it is a genuine listing site, not dead. It is part of the same confirmed licensedata.org network as californiabrokers.org, californiaengineering.org, californialicensing.org, californianursing.org, californiapharmacists.org, and dentistscalifornia.org (site footer links to 'California Cosmetology / Dentists / Firearms Permits / Engineering / Brokers'). WebFetch of the homepage did not surface removal info, but fetching /contact directly (via curl with a browser user-agent) returned the full page including two Cloudflare-obfuscated email spans (cdn-cgi/l/email-protection data-cfemail hex payloads); decoding them with the standard single-byte XOR scheme yielded removals@licensedata.org and contact@licensedata.org -- the same operator addresses used across the rest of the network. Page text confirms: 'We understand that in certain circumstances a licensee may want to be removed from the site... To proceed with removal, email removals@licensedata.org. Please include the ID of your record, which is shown on the bottom right corner of your license details block.' No CAPTCHA/ID/phone gate described -> tier:auto, method:email. people_search left false (professional license registry, not general identity/address lookup), priority:high given public named-individual license records plus reviews and a narrow email-only removal path. opt_out_url left null since removal requires locating your own listing first rather than a fixed landing page.
brokers.instructions_md:
1. Go to https://www.alarmscalifornia.org/ and search for your own name or your alarm company's name to find your license listing.
2. Open your listing and note the record ID shown in the bottom-right corner of the license-details block -- you'll need this for the removal request.
3. Email removals@licensedata.org and include the record ID plus your full name (or business name) as it appears on the listing, asking that your record be removed from alarmscalifornia.org.
4. Note that the site explicitly warns removal may make it harder for others to verify your license through this particular (unofficial) site -- your official license status remains verifiable through California's Bureau of Security and Investigative Services regardless.
5. Because this site is part of a shared network (californiabrokers.org, californiaengineering.org, californialicensing.org, californianursing.org, californiapharmacists.org, dentistscalifornia.org, and others) run by the same operator, a removal request to removals@licensedata.org may need to be repeated separately for each site where you or your business has a separate listing -- check the related-registry links in the site footer.

Equifax's Privacy Preference Center at the myprivacy.equifax.com URL lets a consumer, without creating an account: (a) exercise Right to Know/Access, Right to Delete, and Right to Correct on personal info Equifax holds, and (b) exercise Right to Limit Use, Right to Opt-Out (stop Equifax selling/sharing personal info to third parties), and Right to Opt-In. The page states requests are free of charge, no account is required, but the consumer must supply personal information to complete the request, and standard requests are completed within 45 days per applicable law. A phone alternative is offered for consumers 18+: 1-866-295-6801 (Consumer Care, 9am-9pm ET Mon-Fri, 9am-6pm ET Sat/Sun). Separate downloadable mail-in forms exist for requests made on behalf of a minor, an incapacitated adult, or by an authorized agent. brokers.instructions_md:

2. Choose the request type: use "Right to Know/Access, Right to Delete, and Right to Correct" if you want to see, delete, or fix personal information Equifax holds, or use "Right to Limit Use, Opt-Out, and Opt-In" if you specifically want Equifax to stop selling or sharing your personal information with third parties.
3. Follow the guided form, supplying your name, address, and contact information so Equifax can locate your record and respond to you -- there is no fee for any of these requests.

7. This CCPA opt-out is separate from two other Equifax tools you may also want: the free federal prescreen opt-out at optoutprescreen.com (stops pre-approved credit/insurance offer mailings from all four bureaus) and a security freeze on your Equifax credit report (restricts new-credit access to your file) -- neither is a substitute for the other.

The policy explicitly notes 'Any background check data regulated by the Fair Credit Reporting Act is exempt from CCPA data rights requests' -- meaning most of what this company holds on a given person is NOT reachable via a standard CCPA opt-out, only the residual non-FCRA personal data Inflection processes as a business. This is a meaningful caveat: consumers seeking to dispute or remove background-check content need the FCRA dispute process (typically via the employer/requesting party), not a CCPA opt-out. Listed dpo@inflection.com as the opt-out contact per the fetched privacy policy (legal@inflection.com given as an alternate); no dedicated self-serve opt-out URL was found in the fetched content, so opt_out_url is null. tier set to guided (method:email would normally imply auto, but the FCRA-exemption caveat means this isn't a simple no-strings email opt-out -- flagged guided given real complexity) and method left as email since that's the only channel confirmed.
brokers.instructions_md:
1. Understand the scope first: most of what Inflection/GoodHire holds is FCRA-regulated background-check data (criminal, education, motor-vehicle, credit history) obtained for an employer or other requesting party, and that category is exempt from standard state privacy opt-out rights. If you're disputing a background-check report specifically, use the FCRA dispute process referenced in the report itself (usually via the company that ordered the check), not the steps below.
2. For any other personal data Inflection holds outside that FCRA-regulated background-check context, email dpo@inflection.com (or legal@inflection.com) and state you are requesting deletion/opt-out of the sale or sharing of your personal information under applicable state privacy law.
3. Include your full name and the email address(es) associated with any account or check you believe involved you, so Inflection can locate your record.
4. Alternatively, call 1-855-278-7451 to reach Inflection's privacy team, or send a written request to Inflection Risk Solutions, LLC, Attn: Privacy Team, 1 Montgomery St. Ste 2400, San Francisco, CA 94104.
5. Inflection may need to verify your identity before acting on the request.

brokers.instructions_md:
1. Innovis does not run its own separate 'opt out of data sale' web form for consumers the way some other bureaus do -- its consumer-facing privacy notice (routed from innovis.com to business.innovis.com) states its CCPA opt-out section applies only to business-to-business relationships, since Innovis says it does not sell or share consumer personal information for direct marketing to third parties in a way that would trigger a separate opt-out.
2. To stop creditors and insurers from receiving your name on marketing lists for unsolicited "firm offer" credit/insurance mail (the main consumer-facing list Innovis and the other three bureaus maintain), use the shared joint-bureau opt-out at https://www.optoutprescreen.com/ or call 1-888-567-8688. This is the mechanism Innovis's own site directs consumers to.
3. If your concern is restricting access to your Innovis credit file for new-credit applications (identity-theft protection rather than marketing), use Innovis's security freeze tool instead, at innovis.com/personal/securityFreeze, or call 1-866-712-4546; this is a different product from a data-sale opt-out.
4. For general consumer assistance, including questions about your Innovis file or privacy inquiries not covered by the above, call 1-800-540-2505, or write to Innovis Consumer Assistance, PO Box 530088, Atlanta, GA 30353-0088.
5. Do not email Innovis with personal information for these requests -- their own privacy notice specifically asks that inquiries not be submitted by email, to protect the confidentiality of your data.
6. If you believe information in your Innovis credit report itself is inaccurate, that is a separate dispute process (not a privacy opt-out): use your online Innovis account, call 1-866-712-0021, or mail an Investigation Request form to the same Atlanta PO Box.

brokers.name: AmRent
brokers.notes: WebFetched amrent.com/privacy and amrent.com/consumer_assistance directly; both loaded and confirmed the process described below. AmRent is a tenant/resident-screening consumer reporting agency (used by landlords, integrated into Rent Manager and similar property-management software), not a classic address/people-search broker despite the legacy CSV's 'People Search' tag. Its own privacy notice states it is exempt from CCPA-style opt-out because it is a consumer reporting agency governed by FCRA/GLBA instead -- 'If you submit your request to us, we may deny the request' for requests that should go to the landlord/data controller. There is no 'opt out of sale' mechanism; the only real consumer-facing rights are FCRA file access and dispute, via phone, mail, or downloadable Consumer Dispute Form / Request My Report Form (no online portal, no email intake -- email is explicitly discouraged). No fee. No government ID required for a standard report/dispute request (ID is only required for the separate human-trafficking-block process). Because the actual lever available to consumers is dispute/access rather than removal, and the site is FCRA-exempt from CCPA, priority is standard rather than crucial; tier is guided because it's phone/mail/form-only with no self-service portal.
brokers.instructions_md:
1. AmRent does not offer a self-service "opt out of sale" -- as an FCRA-regulated tenant-screening company, it is exempt from that kind of request, and if you submit one anyway it may be denied.
2. If you were denied housing or want to see what's in your AmRent tenant-screening report, request your free copy by mail or fax: download the "Request My Report Form" from [amrent.com/privacy](http://www.amrent.com/privacy) or [amrent.com/consumer_assistance](http://www.amrent.com/consumer_assistance), fill it out, and mail it to AmRent Consumer Assistance, PO Box 530091, Atlanta, GA 30353 (or call to ask about faxing it).
3. To dispute inaccurate information on your report, use the "Consumer Dispute Form" from the same pages and submit it the same way (mail/fax); AmRent will investigate and correct or remove disputed items.
4. You can also call AmRent Consumer Assistance at 888-898-6196 with questions about a report or dispute.
5. If a landlord or property manager denied your application based on an AmRent report, that decision was made by them, not AmRent -- follow up with the landlord directly, since AmRent can't approve or deny applications itself.
6. Email (consumers@amrent.com) exists but AmRent's own materials discourage using it for sensitive requests -- prefer phone or mail.

brokers.name: California Contractors (licensedata.org network)
brokers.notes: Prior pass flagged this as possibly out of scope (a genuine CA contractor-license lookup, 329,542 licensed contractors, 'similar to a state licensing board'). Fetched contractorscalifornia.org/contact directly (with a browser user-agent; plain curl was Cloudflare-challenged) and confirmed it is NOT an official government site -- it is part of the same unofficial licensedata.org network already documented for californiabrokers.org, californiaengineering.org, californialicensing.org, californianursing.org, californiapharmacists.org, and dentistscalifornia.org. The page's own FAQ says its data is 'from official government records, in some cases supplemented by other data sources' -- i.e. it republishes CSLB license data with its own UI, reviews, and removal flow, it is not the CSLB itself. Its footer lists sibling sites: California Security, California Pharmacists, California Dentists, California Engineering, Alarms California. Decoded the page's Cloudflare email-obfuscation (data-cfemail hex payloads) independently and recovered removals@licensedata.org (removal requests) and contact@licensedata.org (general inquiries) -- same shared operator/backend as the rest of the network. Site explicitly discourages delisting ('doing so will prevent others from verifying your license') but the removal-by-email process is real and described in the page text, identified by a per-record ID shown on each listing. people_search:true (publishes named individuals' license, contact, and standing records with reviews) matching the dentistscalifornia.org precedent in this same network; priority:standard rather than crucial since it's a narrow professional-license registry, not a general address/phone reseller. opt_out_url left null because there is no single fixed opt-out landing page -- the flow requires locating your own listing first.
brokers.instructions_md:
1. Go to contractorscalifornia.org and search for your name or business to find your listing.
2. Open your listing and note the record ID shown in the bottom-right corner of the license-details block.
3. Email removals@licensedata.org with that record ID and a request to remove your listing.
4. The site discourages delisting, arguing it prevents others from verifying your contractor license -- your official license status remains verifiable through the California Contractors State License Board (CSLB) directly regardless of what you decide here.
5. This site is part of a shared network (California Brokers, California Engineering, California Licensing, California Nursing, California Pharmacists, California Dentists, California Security, Alarms California, and others) run by the same operator behind licensedata.org -- if you hold other licenses, you may need to repeat this removal request separately for each site where you're listed.
6. If you don't hear back, follow up using contact@licensedata.org, referencing your original removal request.
